title: Request Chronology & Filter Composer (trace-to-span drilldown prototype)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a polished, testable prototype for an integrated Request Chronology view that lets operators traverse from a high-level request card into span-level timelines and back, compose complex filter queries (by correlation ID, service, span kind, error state, tokenized time ranges), and persist filters as named views for alerting dashboards and rollout debug sessions. This design ties into the Console rollout workspace: engineers should be able to open an active rollout and jump to correlated requests across regions and model variants.
proposed_solution: Build a three-pane prototype: (1) left: compact request list with correlation ID tags and quick status badges; (2) center: request chronology timeline that flattens spans into an adjustable time scale with stacked lanes per service; (3) right: filter composer with live-preview counts and an example query language conversion (human-readable <-> query DSL). Interactions: link correlation IDs to cross-request scatter, hover to preview span details, click to expand span to full stack trace and payload preview. Provide a compact savour view to surface cost-attribution per request (token counts, model variant), and a 'jump to rollout' button when the request is part of a canary/AB rollout. Prototype must include keyboard-driven navigation and accessible color contrasts for error/warn/info states.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows three-pane layout with left request list, central timeline and right filter composer
Filters support correlation_id, service, span_kind, status_code, duration (> / <), and time window; live counts update as filters are changed
Clicking a span opens a detail overlay with full span metadata, example payload, and link to associated GitHub PR/trace session when available
Named filter views can be saved locally in prototype (simulate persistence) and exported as permalink for console dashboards
Design passes accessibility contrast checks and includes keyboard navigation spec (tab order, aria labels)
Prototype demonstrates a 'jump to rollout' flow from a request associated with an active rollout and shows model variant and cost estimate

mockup_notes: Timeline scales non-linearly: microsecond events shown at 1x, long blocking spans compress with a visual crumb to preserve context
Span lanes collapse identical consecutive spans with a counter badge to reduce vertical noise
Correlation IDs appear as pill UI with copy button and cross-request quick-open (⌘/Ctrl+Click to open in new tab)
Filter composer shows immediate tokenized DSL below human-friendly builder; toggling shows both representations
Cost chip derives from token_estimate metadata; show approximate USD and hover for breakdown by model variant
When a request is part of a rollout, show rollout tag with percent exposure and 'open rollout' CTA linking to the rollout panel
ux_considerations: Performance: timeline must stream and paginate gracefully; prototype will simulate streaming and show loading placeholders
Information density: provide compact and expanded density toggles; default to compact for large result sets
Onboarding: include brief tooltip tour for first-time users explaining filter composer and 'jump to rollout' flow
Privacy: truncate request payloads by default and provide reveal controls for PII-sensitive fields (requires eng flags)
Sync with Console color tokens to ensure consistent severity colors across console products
risks_and_tradeoffs: Full persistence of named views increases backend scope; prototype will emulate persistence and hand off API contract to ENG
Showing cost estimates per-request requires token accounting which can be noisy; use conservative approximations and clear 'estimate' label
Aggressive timeline compression may hide causal relationships; include a focus+context mode to expand around selected spans
Canonical query DSL can be hard for less technical users; keep the human builder primary and allow advanced users to switch to DSL
